title: Two separate ways of wiping and refilling the phone on a restore, kept in step by hand
what: Restoring a new backup file uses one list of what to clear on the phone, while restoring an old Drive backup and the safety copy taken before a Drive restore use a second, older list. When a new kind of data is added, it must be added to both lists or one kind of restore will leave old data behind or lose it.
expected: One shared rule for what a restore clears and brings back, used by every kind of restore and by the safety copy.
how_often: only after a new kind of data is added and one list is missed
fix_line: Make the old Drive restore and the safety copy use the same clear-and-refill list as the new backup file

title: Restore screen can say this phone has 0 workouts when it simply could not count them
what: Before a member replaces everything on the phone with a backup, the screen shows how many workouts, folders and measurements the phone has now. If the count fails, the error is swallowed and the screen shows 0, so the member may replace the phone thinking nothing will be lost.
expected: When the phone's contents cannot be counted, say so (or do not show numbers) instead of showing 0.
how_often: rare, only when the phone database read fails
fix_line: Show 'could not check' instead of 0 when the count fails, and log the error

title: Backup code uses its own date rules, one of them on world time instead of India time
what: A progress photo restored without a date is given today's date on world time, so between midnight and 5:30 am in India it lands on yesterday. The backup file name also uses its own copy of the phone-date rule instead of the app's shared one.
expected: Every date in backup and restore comes from the app's one shared phone-date rule.
how_often: rare, a dateless photo restored after midnight
fix_line: Use the app's shared today rule in both places

title: Some Google Drive and gym-sync failures vanish without any trace
what: Setting up Google sign-in for Drive, checking the Drive user, signing out of Drive and sending the old gym summary when the internet returns all throw their errors away without writing anything to the log, so a support person has nothing to go on when they fail.
expected: Every caught failure writes at least one warning line to the log.
who: support, when a member reports a Drive problem
fix_line: Add a warning log line to each of these caught failures

title: Switched-off coach, old gym link and Drive upload code stays in the app with no tests
what: The AI coach with its own key (switched off), the old email gym link and its sync (switched off) and the Drive upload (no screen uses it) are all still in the app. No test opens the coach's chat engine, the three AI services, the gym sync queue, the internet watcher or the summary builder, so if any of these is switched back on nobody knows whether it still works.
expected: Code that is switched off either gets removed or keeps tests that prove it still works before it is switched back on.
who: the team, when a switched-off feature comes back
how_often: each time one of these is switched back on
fix_line: Remove the old gym link and Drive upload code, and add tests for the coach before it is switched on
